questions.question: The iconic seated stone statuette commonly labelled as the 'Priest-King' from Mohenjodaro was carved from which material?
options: A) Steatite
B) Granite
C) Sandstone
D) Marble
questions.explanation: The famous seated male sculpture recovered at Mohenjodaro was carved out of soft soapstone known as steatite.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: Which Greek ambassador was dispatched by Seleucus I Nicator to the Mauryan court of Chandragupta Maurya in Pataliputra?
options: A) Deimachus
B) Megasthenes
C) Dionysius
D) Strabo
questions.explanation: Megasthenes was the Hellenistic diplomat sent by Seleucus Nicator who recorded his observations in the work Indica.

questions.question: According to ancient Dharmashastras and the Manusmriti, what did the term 'Stridhana' denote?
options: A) Ancestral land exclusively inherited by eldest daughters
B) Taxes collected from female merchants
C) Presents and valuables received by a woman at the time of her marriage
D) Fines imposed on women for violating caste boundaries
questions.explanation: Stridhana referred to the wealth and gifts given to a woman on the occasion of her wedding, over which she retained special ownership rights.

questions.question: At which holy site did Siddhartha Gautama attain enlightenment beneath the sacred pipal tree?
options: A) Lumbini
B) Sarnath
C) Kushinagar
D) Bodh Gaya
questions.explanation: Siddhartha attained supreme spiritual enlightenment at Bodh Gaya in modern Bihar, becoming known as the Buddha.

questions.question: Abu Rayhan al-Biruni composed his monumental encyclopedic treatise 'Kitab al-Hind' in which language?
options: A) Arabic
B) Persian
C) Turkish
D) Sanskrit
questions.explanation: Al-Biruni wrote his vast analytical study of Indian religion, philosophy, mathematics, and customs in Arabic.

questions.question: Which specialized tool discovery at craft-production sites like Chanhudaro, Lothal, and Dholavira confirmed local bead perforation technologies?
options: A) Rotary iron lathe blades
B) Specialized stone drill bits
C) Diamond-tipped blowpipes
D) High-pressure hydraulic nozzles
questions.explanation: Ernest Mackay and subsequent excavators found specialized stone drills designed for perforating micro-beads of carnelian and steatite.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: The Buddhist philosophical text 'Milindapanho' records a theological dialogue between the monk Nagasena and which Indo-Greek ruler?
options: A) Demetrius
B) Antialcidas
C) Menander I
D) Eucratides
questions.explanation: Milindapanho ('Questions of Milinda') captures discussions between the Buddhist sage Nagasena and King Menander I.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: In the Allahabad Pillar inscription (Prayag Prashasti), what specific imperial policy did Samudragupta adopt towards the twelve defeated kings of Dakshinapatha?
options: A) Annexing their territories directly into central provincial administration
B) Banishing their entire lineages across the Indian Ocean
C) Executing their military commandants and confiscating temple lands
D) Capturing and subsequently releasing them to rule as tributary vassals (Grahan-Moksha-Anugraha)
questions.explanation: Harishena records that Samudragupta defeated the kings of Dakshinapatha, accepted their homage, and restored them as tributary rulers.

questions.question: Under the leadership of which prominent Sanskrit scholar was the ambitious Critical Edition of the Mahabharata initiated by the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute in 1919?
options: A) V.S. Sukthankar
B) Suniti Kumar Chatterji
C) Bhandarkar Devadatta
D) K.A. Nilakanta Sastri
questions.explanation: Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar supervised the team of scholars who collated hundreds of regional manuscripts to construct the critical edition.

questions.question: According to the Pali Buddhist texts, who was a 'Gahapati' in the socio-economic structure of early historical India?
options: A) A wandering ascetic bound by vows of severe austerities
B) The master and head of a household who possessed land, cattle, and urban wealth
C) An untouchable artisan residing outside village palisades
D) A royal courtier entrusted with frontier fortifications
questions.explanation: In Pali literature, a gahapati was the prosperous proprietor and manager of agrarian and domestic assets.

questions.question: Which princely rulers of Bhopal provided crucial funds, conservation assistance, and accommodation for European and Indian researchers at Sanchi?
options: A) Sikandar Lodi and Qudsia Begum
B) Jahanara Begum and Nur Jahan
C) Shahjehan Begum and Sultan Jehan Begum
D) Begum Hazrat Mahal and Zeb-un-Nissa
questions.explanation: The Begums of Bhopal financed the museum, guesthouse, and monumental volumes by John Marshall, preserving the Great Stupa.

questions.question: The 'Therigatha' holds a unique place in world religious literature because it is composed entirely of:
options: A) Sanskrit invocations chanted exclusively during Vedic horse sacrifices
B) Monastic rules authored by Emperor Ashoka for Sri Lankan monks
C) Debates between court physicians regarding herbal medicinal treatises
D) Verses and hymns created by Buddhist bhikkhunis expressing spiritual liberation
questions.explanation: The Therigatha is an anthology of Pali poems authored by senior Buddhist nuns (theris) describing their inner journey to nirvana.

questions.question: In his travel memoir, Ibn Battuta noted that the state postal communications in 14th-century India utilized two distinct systems: the horse-post and the foot-post. What was the foot-post called?
options: A) Dawa
B) Uluq
C) Kharaj
D) Barid
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta recorded that the horse-post was called uluq and the faster foot-courier post was called dawa, having three stops per mile.

questions.question: To which European monarch did the French physician Francois Bernier dedicate his principal treatise 'Travels in the Mogul Empire'?
options: A) King Charles II
B) King Louis XIV
C) Emperor Philip II
D) King Gustavus Adolphus
questions.explanation: Francois Bernier dedicated his travels and letters comparing Mughal landholding unfavourably with European private property to King Louis XIV.

questions.question: The religious anthology 'Nalayira Divyaprabandham' frequently hailed as the Tamil Veda was composed by which devotional group?
options: A) The sixty-three Shaivite Nayanar saints
B) The Virashaiva vachanakaras of Kalyana
C) The twelve Vaishnavite Alvar saints
D) The Nathpanthi yogis of Gorakhpur
questions.explanation: The Nalayira Divyaprabandham was the anthology of 4,000 Tamil verses composed by the Alvars and compiled by Nathamuni.

questions.question: Who was the female Alvar saint whose impassioned Tamil love poems expressed her devotion and spiritual longing for Vishnu as her beloved?
options: A) Karaikkal Ammaiyar
B) Avvaiyar
C) Akkamahadevi
D) Andal
questions.explanation: Andal, the only female Alvar, envisioned herself as the bride of Lord Ranganatha (Vishnu).

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: Which Vijayanagara emperor authored the celebrated Telugu political treatise 'Amuktamalyada' detailing statecraft and maritime commerce?
options: A) Krishnadeva Raya
B) Deva Raya II
C) Harihara II
D) Achyuta Deva Raya
questions.explanation: Krishnadeva Raya of the Tuluva dynasty composed Amuktamalyada, in which he prescribed policies for royal revenue, ports, and foreign merchants.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: The Hazara Rama temple complex located within the Royal Centre of Vijayanagara was designated primarily for:
options: A) Public assemblies and mass wedding ceremonies of merchants
B) The private worship of the monarch and the imperial household
C) The initiation rites of foreign mercenary cavalrymen
D) Granary storage during monsoons
questions.explanation: The Hazara Rama temple was the private sanctuary for the king and his family, adorned with sculpted bas-reliefs illustrating the Ramayana.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In the revenue classification of agricultural soils during Akbar's reign, what was the term for land that remained continuously under cultivation and was never fallow?
options: A) Parauti
B) Chachar
C) Polaj
D) Banjar
questions.explanation: The Ain-i-Akbari classifies agricultural land into four categories: Polaj was annually cultivated without fallow intervals.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In the administrative hierarchy of Mughal villages, which official maintained the detailed village accounts of crop yields and peasant tax payments?
options: A) Muqaddam
B) Amil-guzar
C) Qanungo
D) Patwari
questions.explanation: The Patwari was the village accountant who kept meticulous fiscal registers of lands, yields, and assessments.

questions.question: The violent Santhal uprising of 1855-1856 in the Damin-i-Koh forest tract was spearheaded by which brother duo?
options: A) Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu
B) Birsa and Sugana Munda
C) Titu Mir and Haji Shariatullah
D) Rani Gaidinliu and Jadonang
questions.explanation: Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu mobilized thousands of Santhal peasants against rapacious moneylenders (dikus) and British revenue authorities.

questions.question: During the uprising of 1857, which septuagenarian landlord organized guerrilla operations against British forces across Arrah and western Bihar?
options: A) Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah
B) Kunwar Singh
C) Bakht Khan
D) Tatya Tope
questions.explanation: Kunwar Singh, the elderly zamindar of Jagdishpur, provided bold military leadership in Bihar during 1857.

questions.question: The historic Dandi Salt March commenced from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930 and reached the coastal village of Dandi after spanning how many days?
options: A) 14 days
B) 35 days
C) 24 days
D) 40 days
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi and his 78 satyagrahi companions marched 240 miles over 24 days, breaking the salt law on 6 April 1930.

questions.question: At which Indian National Congress session was the declaration of 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) formally adopted under Jawaharlal Nehru's presidency?
options: A) Karachi Session (March 1931)
B) Belgaum Session (December 1924)
C) Calcutta Session (September 1920)
D) Lahore Session (December 1929)
questions.explanation: The December 1929 Lahore session of the Congress proclaimed Purna Swaraj as its goal and unfurled the tricolour flag on the banks of the Ravi.

questions.question: Who served as the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly, preparing comparative analyses of foreign democratic constitutions?
options: A) Sir B.N. Rau
B) Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha
C) K.M. Munshi
D) S.N. Mukherjee
questions.explanation: Sir Benegal Narsing Rau served as the legal and constitutional advisor, compiling initial working drafts for the Assembly.

questions.question: Regarding the decline of the Mature Harappan urban centers, which archaeological evidence disproved Mortimer Wheeler's hypothesis of an 'Aryan massacre' at Mohenjodaro?
options: A) The discovery of Greek artillery shells buried under the Citadel platform
B) Stratigraphic analysis showing human skeletal remains belonged to multiple, non-contemporaneous geological strata with no signs of military assault
C) Charred wooden barricades containing iron swords dated to the third millennium BCE
D) Inscriptions in cuneiform recording peace treaties signed by Harappan and Aryan kings
questions.explanation: Archaeologist George Dales re-examined the stratigraphy of Mohenjodaro skeletal finds, proving they were interred at different time periods and lacked battlefield wounds.

questions.question:
Arrange the following milestones in Harappan archaeological discoveries in correct chronological order:
1. Daya Ram Sahni unearths seals at Harappa
2. Alexander Cunningham publishes the first known Harappan seal
3. John Marshall officially announces the discovery of the Indus Valley Civilisation to the world
4. R.E.M. Wheeler begins strategic stratigraphic excavations at Harappa as Director-General
questions.explanation: Cunningham published the seal in 1875; Sahni excavated Harappa in 1921; Marshall announced the discovery in 1924; Wheeler began his deep trench excavations in 1944.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: The Junagadh rock inscription of the Western Kshatrapa ruler Rudradaman I (c. 150 CE) claims exceptional administrative virtue on what grounds?
options: A) He completely prohibited maritime navigation across the Gulf of Khambhat
B) He converted the Mauryan royal granaries into Buddhist viharas
C) He conquered Sri Lanka and erected bilingual Greek-Brahmi pillars
D) He financed the reconstruction of the breached Sudarshana Lake dam from his own royal treasury without levying emergency taxes (vishti) on his subjects
questions.explanation: Rudradaman boasted that he repaired the Lake Sudarshana embankment entirely from private royal funds without imposing oppressive taxes or forced labour (vishti).

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: In early historical Tamil society depicted in Sangam poetry, who were the 'Adimai' and 'Vellalar' respectively?
options: A) Slaves/bonded labourers and large landowners
B) Royal charioteers and hill-dwelling pastoralists
C) Temple priests and wandering bardic musicians
D) Gold-washers and foreign horse traders
questions.explanation: Sangam literature categorizes southern agrarian society into Vellalar (wealthy landowners), Uzhavar (ploughmen), and Adimai (slaves/bonded labourers).

questions.question: The dynastic marital practices of the Satavahana rulers of the Deccan violated orthodox Brahmanical gotra prescriptions in which of the following ways?
options: A) They exclusively contracted marriages with Persian princesses
B) Satavahana queens retained their paternal gotras (such as Gotama and Vasithi) after marriage and practiced clan endogamy
C) They adopted matrilineal inheritance where sons took their mother's personal names as throne titles without gotras
D) They abandoned all Vedic sacrificial rituals in favour of Hellenistic mystery cults
questions.explanation: Brahmanical Dharmashastras mandated gotra exogamy, whereas Satavahana inscriptional evidence shows queens retained their father's gotra and married within the clan.

questions.question: The Buddhist narrative of the 'Matanga Jataka' primarily critiques contemporary social orthodoxies by portraying:
options: A) A warrior king who renounced his empire to become a sea-faring spice merchant
B) A wealthy merchant who constructed stone aqueducts across the Vindhyan plateau
C) A Bodhisatta born as a Chandala who morally exposed the spiritual arrogance of high-caste Brahman scholars
D) A sage who proved that women were incapable of attaining moral virtue
questions.explanation: The Matanga Jataka tells the tale of Matanga, an outcast Chandala Bodhisatta whose moral integrity humbled orthodox Brahmans.

questions.question: In the structural anatomy of early Buddhist stupas, what was the 'Harmika'?
options: A) The circular circumambulatory walkway surrounding the stone railing at ground level
B) The ornamental ceremonial gateway adorned with narrative sculptural panels
C) The subterranean stone vault housing bronze reliquary caskets
D) A balcony-like square enclosure situated atop the hemispherical mound (anda) representing the celestial abode of the gods
questions.explanation: Arising above the rounded dome (anda) was the harmika, a balcony-like square structure symbolising the sacred residence of divine beings.

questions.question: Which crucial doctrinal schism occurred during the Second Buddhist Council held at Vaishali around a century after the Buddha's Parinirvana?
options: A) The split between the orthodox Sthaviravadins (Theravadins) and the liberal Mahasanghikas over ten points of monastic discipline
B) The total repudiation of the concept of rebirth by followers of Sarvastivada
C) The adoption of Tantric Vajrayana rituals by the Pala court
D) The formal compilation of the Abhidhamma Pitaka into written Prakrit texts
questions.explanation: The Council at Vaishali saw early monastic discord regarding disciplinary relaxation (dasavatthuni), dividing the Sangha into Mahasanghikas and Sthaviravadins.

questions.question: Al-Biruni identified three principal impediments that restricted foreigners from easily comprehending Indian society. Which of the following was explicitly one of those barriers?
options: A) The total absence of indigenous astronomical treatises or paper manuscripts
B) The profound linguistic divergence between Sanskrit and Arabic/Persian in expressing abstract philosophical nuances
C) The aggressive proselytisation campaigns conducted by urban Buddhist monasteries
D) The state embargo preventing foreign scholars from travelling beyond port cities
questions.explanation: Al-Biruni highlighted three barriers: the complex Sanskrit language, religious divergences, and the cultural insularity/intellectual aloofness of local scholars.

questions.question: The 16th-century Portuguese traveler Duarte Barbosa composed detailed accounts of southern India that were particularly valuable for their insights into:
options: A) Mughal revenue assessment techniques in Kashmir valleys
B) Sufi meditative breathing techniques practiced in Bengal khanqahs
C) Coastal commercial networks, port duties, gemstone processing, and textiles in the Vijayanagara realm
D) Underground lead-mining corporations in the Aravalli hills
questions.explanation: Duarte Barbosa left rich descriptions of commercial life, trade in spices and precious stones, and maritime mercantile communities.

questions.question: Within the architectural layout of a major medieval Chishti hospice (khanqah), what was the function of the 'Jama'at Khana'?
options: A) A secluded subterranean chamber restricted solely to the senior Shaikh for solitary 40-day fasts
B) A royal treasure vault designated for storing state pensions and cash gifts
C) An outdoor courtyard reserved for trial combat between rival Sufi orders
D) A spacious communal hall where disciples, visiting travelers, and dervishes lived, slept, and prayed collectively
questions.explanation: The Jama'at Khana in Nizamuddin Auliya's hospice was the large collective living and prayer room where everyone shared meals and floor space.

questions.question: In Sufism, the musical assembly 'Sama' was practiced with which specific spiritual intention?
options: A) Evoking divine ecstasy and mystical absorption through the listening of sacred poetry sung by musicians
B) Testing the physical endurance of newly admitted novice disciples through dance
C) Commemorating the battlefield victories of regional sultans
D) Enforcing orthodox theological compliance across Sunni jurists
questions.explanation: Sama was the audition or musical performance intended to stimulate divine love and spiritual ecstasy (wajd) in listeners.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: In the catastrophic battle of Rakshasi-Tangadi (Talikota) in 1565 that shattered the power of Vijayanagara, who was the chief minister who commanded the imperial army?
options: A) Sadashiva Raya
B) Rama Raya
C) Tirumala Raya
D) Venkata II
questions.explanation: The de facto ruler and regent minister Rama Raya led the Vijayanagara army into battle against the combined forces of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, and Golconda.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: What archaeological evidence discovered atop the stone platform of the Mahanavami Dibba in Vijayanagara indicates the nature of its original superstructure?
options: A) Subterranean bronze pipes that circulated refrigerated water to royal swimming pools
B) Monolithic granite pillars inscribed with bilingual Latin-Persian treaties
C) Densely arranged post-holes indicating a magnificent multi-tiered wooden pavilion that has since perished
D) Cylindrical brick stupa drums decorated with terracotta figures of Bodhisattvas
questions.explanation: Deep post-holes carved into the stone base prove that the Mahanavami Dibba supported a multi-storeyed wooden structure used for royal rituals.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In the textual structure of Abu'l Fazl's 'Ain-i-Akbari', which book (daftar) contains the detailed fiscal, agricultural, and administrative statistics of the twelve subahs?
options: A) Manzil-Abadi
B) Sipah-Abadi
C) Ruqqa-i-Alamgiri
D) Mulk-Abadi
questions.explanation: The Ain-i-Akbari is divided into five books: Manzil-Abadi deals with royal household; Sipah-Abadi with military/civil; Mulk-Abadi contains provincial revenue data.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: Which monetary reform initiated by Sher Shah Suri was adopted and standardized throughout the Mughal Empire, establishing the standard silver currency?
options: A) The silver Rupiya weighing approximately 178 grains
B) The bronze Tanka weighing 80 grains
C) The gold Mohur weighing 250 grains
D) The copper Dam weighing 50 grains
questions.explanation: Sher Shah introduced the pure silver Rupiya (178 grains) which became the standard silver monetary unit of Mughal India.

questions.question: Under the regulations of the Permanent Settlement in Bengal (1793), what was the operational effect of the draconian 'Sunset Law'?
options: A) Peasants were forbidden from cultivating their holdings after twilight hours
B) If the zamindar failed to remit the fixed revenue before sunset on the appointed due date, his estate was liable to immediate public auction
C) Village headmen were arrested if evening village curfew was breached
D) Moneylenders were prohibited from recovering interest debts after sundown
questions.explanation: The Sunset Law mandated that if payment was not deposited by sunset on the scheduled date, the government would auction the zamindari land.

questions.question: The Deccan Riots Commission report submitted to the British Parliament in 1878 concluded that peasant violence in Ahmednagar and Poona was primarily provoked by:
options: A) Forced conversion policies enforced by British evangelical missionaries in village schools
B) The prohibition of indigenous iron-smelting furnaces by the forest department
C) The manipulation of credit accounts, debt bonds, and extortionate interest rates by moneylenders following the collapse of the cotton boom
D) The compulsory recruitment of ryots into the Royal Indian Navy for service in Burma
questions.explanation: The Commission revealed that the fall of global cotton prices after the American Civil War trapped peasants in inescapable cycles of debt manipulated by sahukars.

questions.question: The famous Azamgarh Proclamation issued on 25 August 1857 under the name of Feroz Shah appealed to which collective sentiment across north India?
options: A) An endorsement of British land tenure reforms in return for religious non-interference
B) A demand for the annexation of the Punjab by the Nawab of Awadh
C) A plea for Russian military intervention via the Khyber Pass
D) A passionate call for communal unity between Hindus and Muslims across all social classes to expel British colonial rule
questions.explanation: The Azamgarh Proclamation emphasized Hindu-Muslim brotherhood, addressing zamindars, merchants, civil servants, and artisans to resist British exploitation.

questions.question: The Victorian oil painting 'In Memoriam' painted in 1858 by Joseph Noel Paton created widespread emotional hysteria in Britain by depicting:
options: A) Defenceless British women and children huddled in distress, awaiting death or rescue during the revolt of 1857
B) The heroic counter-charge of the Highland regiment breaching the Kashmiri Gate
C) The ceremonial court trial and exile of Emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar
D) The formal signing of Queen Victoria's proclamation at Allahabad
questions.explanation: Paton's 'In Memoriam' depicted frightened European women and children huddled together in a room, provoking retaliatory fury in England.

questions.question: In which Round Table Conference held in London did Mahatma Gandhi participate as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress?
options: A) First Round Table Conference (1930)
B) Second Round Table Conference (1931)
C) Third Round Table Conference (1932)
D) Joint Parliamentary Select Committee (1934)
questions.explanation: Following the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931, Gandhi travelled to London to attend the Second Round Table Conference representing the Congress.

questions.question: Why did Mahatma Gandhi abruptly suspend the nationwide Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922?
options: A) The British Viceroy agreed to concede Dominion Status unconditionally
B) Subhas Chandra Bose resigned from the civil services to organize the Indian National Army
C) A violent clash occurred at Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur where an enraged crowd set fire to a police station, killing 22 policemen
D) The Khilafat committee dissolved itself after political secularization in Turkey
questions.explanation: Deeply committed to absolute non-violence, Gandhi called off the movement after the violent incident at Chauri Chaura on 4 February 1922.

questions.question: During the language controversies in the Constituent Assembly, which representative from the United Provinces passionately argued that Hindi in Devanagari script must be made the sole national language?
options: A) G. Durgabai
B) Shankarrao Deo
C) Frank Anthony
D) R.V. Dhulekar
questions.explanation: R.V. Dhulekar forcefully insisted in December 1946 and later debates that those who did not know Hindustani/Hindi had no right to remain in the Assembly.

questions.question: In the Constituent Assembly debates on fundamental rights, which nationalist leader firmly denounced separate electorates as 'a poison that has entered the body politic of our country'?
options: A) Jawaharlal Nehru
B) Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
C) Govind Ballabh Pant
D) K.M. Munshi
questions.explanation: Sardar Patel delivered a powerful speech warning that separate electorates had partitioned the nation and would destroy its future if retained.

questions.question: In the debates regarding provincial autonomy versus a strong central union, which prominent member from Madras vigorously advocated for robust central authority to prevent national disintegration?
options: A) Somnath Lahiri
B) B. Pocker Bahadur
C) Jaipal Singh
D) K. Santhanam and Gopalaswami Ayyangar
questions.explanation: Gopalaswami Ayyangar and prominent members insisted on a strong Centre capable of maintaining external security and internal economic unity.
